hypotheses.summary: The output grid is formed by taking the colors from the first column of the input grid and alternating them across the rows of the output grid, while simultaneously alternating the colors from the second row's first column across the columns of the output grid. Specifically, O[r, c] = Input[r, 0] if c is even, and O[r, c] = Input[1-r, 0] if c is odd. This is equivalent to tiling the pattern [C_in_0, C_in_1, C_in_0, C_in_1, ...] across both rows, but swapping the roles of the two input colors bas

The output grid is constructed by alternating the background color of the input grid's rows. Specifically, if the input row 0 has color C_in_0 and row 1 has color C_in_1, the output row 0 will alternate between C_in_0 and C_in_1, starting with C_in_0 at column 0. The output row 1 will alternate between C_in_1 and C_in_0, starting with C_in_1 at column 0.
